We recently announced the introduction of a new ownership model for secondary calendars to improve data governance and lifecycle management. Going forward, each secondary calendar will have a single, dedicated owner and will automatically inherit that owner’s organizational policies. This provides more control for admins to define policies for each calendar. As part of this change, owners have already been automatically assigned to secondary calendars. However, for some calendars, no owner could be determined. In most cases, this indicates that the calendar is abandoned and unused. We’ve provided additional information below to guide you through these upcoming changes. What this means for your organization Key changes: 1) Secondary calendar lifecycle: Going forward, when a user account is deleted, all secondary calendars owned by that user will also be permanently deleted. This change aligns the handling of secondary calendars with that of primary calendars. Additionally, if an account is transferred to another organization, their secondary calendars are deleted. Secondary calendars of accounts deleted from January 2026 onward will be included in the cleanup starting April 27, 2026, unless ownership is transferred to another user. 2) Calendar list in settings: All secondary calendars owned by a user will be displayed in the user’s calendar list in their Calendar settings. An active user with the highest permissions will receive ownership during the transition, thus preventing the calendar from being deleted. Option 2: Use the Data Export tool (formerly domain-wide Takeout) to back up organizational data. For calendars owned by users outside your organization, please instruct your users to use Google Takeout individually. Please be aware that all calendars on the attached list as well as calendars owned by deleted accounts will enter into a data deletion process starting April 27, 2026. Title: Is this legit?
Description: Hi Jack, This a phishing scam, report it and delete it. A " nifty.com Docusign " email is a common and sophisticated phishing scam, where attackers use the legitimate Japanese internet provider's email service to send fake Docusign requests, often bypassing filters because the sending accounts are real. Title: Fwd: [Action Required] Prepare for changes to internal and external classifications in Google Groups
Description: Locally Owned and Family-Oriented, Leading the Multi-Housing Flooring Industry Since 2010 Chino | Las Vegas | Los Angeles | Phoenix | San Diego ---------- Forwarded message --------- From: The Google Workspace Team <workspace-noreply@google.com> Date: Wed, Jan 21, 2026 at 12:19 PM Subject: [Action Required] Prepare for changes to internal and external classifications in Google Groups To: <jim@seamlessflooring.org> Update your API scripts before stricter classifications start in Q2 2026. Dear administrator, We’re writing to inform you that in Q2 2026, we’ll introduce stricter enforcement of internal and external classifications of Google Groups. Currently, groups with the Allow members outside your organization setting disabled can still have external members (added via an admin, via a nested external group, or by changing the group from external to internal, which does not remove existing external members). To ensure better data security and boundary management, this behavior will no longer be supported. We’ve provided additional information below to help you understand this change. What this means for your organization Key changes: To prevent disruption, existing groups with the Allow members outside your organization setting disabled that currently include external members will be automatically updated to a new configuration. These groups will be reclassified as external, but configured so that only admins can add external users (preventing end users from doing so). Additionally, this change will impact multiple UI and API areas within Google Workspace, including: Google Groups (and its usage in other apps like Gmail, Chat and Calendar) Admin console APIs (Cloud Identity, Admin SDK Directory API, Groups Settings API) You can view the complete list of changes and details in this article. Important API behavior change: If you use the Cloud Identity or Admin SDK Directory API to create new groups intended for external members, you may experience script errors if you don’t update your settings. Current behavior: Groups created via API default to allowExternalMembers=False. Currently, admins can add external members to these groups without triggering an error. New behavior: With stricter enforcement, if you attempt to add external members to a group classified as internal (the default setting), the API will reject the request and your script will return an error. What you need to do Action required: If you use these APIs to create groups intended for external members, you need to call the Groups Settings API to update the allowExternalMembers=true setting. If this setting is not updated, attempting to add external members will result in a script error. Timelines: Q2 2026: Enforcement rollout begins. Please ensure your scripts are updated before May 2026. You can start updating your scripts using the Groups Settings API now. Thanks for choosing Google Workspace. – The Google Workspace Team Was this information helpful? © 2026 Google LLC 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043 You have received this important update about your Google Workspace account because you designated this email address as a primary or secondary contact for mandatory service communications in your Google Admin console profile.
Resolution:
Email was to notify that Google Groups will no longer allow External Users to be added to groups. 
A new group, with the External User needs to be created, in order to add an External User to a group.

Title: Refine New Accounts Logic in Sales Pulse
Description: Currently, the New Accounts feature on the Sales Pulse page determines a new account based only on the "Established Date" field. This causes false positives in cases where: A new management company is assigned → the account’s established date updates → Sales Pulse incorrectly flags it as a new account. Requirements: Refine the SQL query logic to check both: Customer Name/Address (to identify the account entity). Whether the account has had previous orders. If an account has prior orders, it should not be considered "new" (instead, classify as "returning"). Only accounts with no prior orders should appear in New Accounts. Outcome: New Accounts reporting will be more accurate by distinguishing true new customers from existing accounts with updated metadata or management changes.
Resolution: The Sales Pulse page has been expanded with two new dashboard sections alongside the monthly performance summary. Users can now track New Account Metrics (showing new accounts, orders, and invoice totals with drill-down property details) and Lost & Returning Customers Analysis (highlighting customers who had a 10+ month gap in activity but have returned, including revenue recovered and rep change details). These additions provide a fuller view of each salesperson’s activity, retention, and account growth.

Title: Add Returning Customers Table
Description: Per request from Dave Nicely, add a feature to measure returning customers. A "returning customer" is defined as an account that has not placed any orders in over 14 months but has now started ordering again. Requirements: Create a new Returning Customers table, similar to the existing New Accounts table. Display key details: Customer Name, Sales Rep, Last Order Date, Returning Order Date, Order Count Since Return, Revenue. Add filtering by date range and sales rep (similar to Sales Pulse filtering). Outcome: Management can track lapsed customers who re-engage, helping sales prioritize follow-ups and monitor customer retention.
Resolution: The Sales Pulse page has been expanded with two new dashboard sections alongside the monthly performance summary. Users can now track New Account Metrics (showing new accounts, orders, and invoice totals with drill-down property details) and Lost & Returning Customers Analysis (highlighting customers who had a 10+ month gap in activity but have returned, including revenue recovered and rep change details).

Title: Add Notes Feature to Tasks
Description: Currently, tasks in SalesMetrics only store the core fields from the task creation form (title, due date, type, etc.). Per request from Dave Nicely, upper management would like the ability to add notes/comments to tasks. Requirements: Add a Notes field to tasks. Notes should be visible to the assigned salesperson in their task list view. Notes should be editable only by managers/admin roles (sales reps can view but not modify). Ensure notes are audit-tracked (CreatedBy, CreatedDate, ModifiedBy, ModifiedDate). Outcome: Managers can leave contextual notes for sales reps that are directly tied to their tasks, improving visibility and accountability.
Resolution: Added full Task Notes functionality to Task.cshtml and AdminTask.cshtml. Each task row now has a Notes button that opens a modal for viewing, adding, editing, and deleting notes. The implementation leverages the existing TaskNote model, along with new controller endpoints for update/delete, and updates GetNotesForTask to exclude deleted notes. Features include real-time refresh, audit tracking (CreatedBy, ModifiedBy, DeletedBy), and role-based permissions (users manage their own notes; admins can manage all).

Title: Fwd: costing sheet change
Description: Locally Owned and Family-Oriented, Leading the Multi-Housing Flooring Industry Since 2010 Chino | Las Vegas | Los Angeles | Phoenix | San Diego ---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Anthony Valente <anthony@seamlessflooring.com> Date: Mon, Aug 11, 2025 at 3:46 PM Subject: costing sheet change To: Jose Solis <jose@seamlessflooring.com>, Chris Workman <chrisw@seamlessflooring.com>, Jim Smith <jsmith@seamlessflooring.org> Hello, I’d like to request a change to the costing sheet functionality. Would it be possible to add an option that allows us to toggle between showing the total amount per line item and displaying only a grand total, similar to how the quantity can be displayed or hidden? The team has been asking for this feature, as many of our other vendors only provide the grand total without line-item price details. Having this option would give us more flexibility in how we present our bids. Please let me know if you need more details or examples to make this change. Thank you, Locally Owned and Family-Oriented, Leading the Multi-Housing Flooring Industry Since 2010 Chino | Las Vegas | Los Angeles | Phoenix | San Diego
Resolution:
Hey Anthony,

The way the current costing sheet is structured, each product’s total is required in order to calculate the grand total for the quote.
This was intentionally developed as a built-in verification step to ensure that the total on the quote matches the sum from the costing sheet.
Removing the per-line totals would require redeveloping the sheet from the ground up, as this check is integrated into the core calculation process.

We do, however, already have the ability to hide quantities for each product line.
This feature can be toggled on the Project Info tab (Row 15, as shown in the screenshot you provided).

While it doesn’t remove the line-item pricing, it does give you the option to limit some of the detail shown to the customer.

Organizations must complete tenant migration to the new Authentication Methods policy before this deadline to avoid significant email and business application interruptions. Missing the deadline may require a support ticket to Microsoft to resolve access issues. View additional details here. Quest’s Recommendation: We strongly encourage you to review the impact of these changes and take the necessary steps to migrate to the new Authentication Methods before the enforcement dates. Quest has developed impact assessment scripts and a migration strategy to help you navigate these changes with minimal disruption. Let me know if you want to talk tech. Always happy to setup a call. Quest has observed a significant increase in targeted social engineering attacks attributed to the threat actor group Shattered Spider, specifically aimed at U.S.-based retail, insurance, staffing, and distribution sectors. These attacks focus on gaining initial access through sophisticated social engineering campaigns, often leading to ransomware deployment and significant operational disruptions. A common scenario consists of the following: Threat actors initiate contact by phone, text, or email, impersonating internal IT or a trusted third party. The threat actor creates urgency with the user, centering on situations such as alleged account compromises or system outages to prompt immediate action. Pressure is then applied to approve MFA requests, access spoofed login portals, or install remote access tools—framing these actions as necessary steps to resolve the issue. Credentials and session tokens are subsequently compromised, enabling full access to Identity Management, MFA, Remote Access, and Email platforms. Quest recommends actively monitoring for unusual help desk activity and ensuring all staff are trained to recognize tactics that use false urgency to manipulate users. Employees should know how to safely verify suspicious requests and escalate concerns. Communicating these risks to your broader user base—especially help desk, finance, and claims teams—is strongly advised. If you would like to discuss detection, prevention, or incident response measures related to this threat, please reply to this email. Did you miss an advisory? Description: Hi Jack, Yes, this is a phishing scam, report it and delete it. Scam Advisory VIP Club Invoice emails Over the last few days we have received a new kind of scam email sent to the "Accounts" email and pretending to be a conversation between the business owner and a 3rd Party about an Advisory VIP Club which has provided Management Advisory Services. The invoices claim to be from a company located at Address: Cromford Mills, Mill Lane, Derbyshire, DE4 3RQ and are for various amounts over £20,000. We have received them from Ion Marion and Elena Petre so far, but as there is little of nothing for anti-phishing AI systems to detect, they are slipping through the net. Both emails we've received have come from US University email addesses, one from MIT.edu and the other from UFL.edu and as they are reaching our inbox rather than scam filter boxes, the emails must be originating from those domains. Below is an extract of one email, but they are both identical in wording. The email claims to come from a @consultant.com email address, but this is just typed, not an actual email: Hello, As requested, please find attached the past-due invoice for Business Coaching and Development, as well as the VIP membership for "business Owner". The Excel Costing Sheet is now functioning as expected.

The main point is that when you go to open the excel file, right click, click on open with and choose Google Sheets. It will auto save as you are making your changes. Thank you, ---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Jose Solis <josesolis@seamlessflooring.com> Date: Wed, Nov 27, 2024 at 9:01 AM Subject: User Guideline: Using Google Shared Files To: Mike Smith <mike@seamlessflooring.com> Cc: Jim Smith <Jim@seamlessflooring.com> Guidelines for Using Google Shared Files To ensure seamless collaboration and prevent data loss or reversion issues when working with shared files on Google Drive, please follow these guidelines: 1. Use Google Sheets in the Browser Always open shared spreadsheets using Google Sheets in your web browser. Google Sheets supports real-time collaboration, allowing multiple users to edit the document simultaneously. All changes are saved automatically. Steps to Open a File in Google Sheets: Navigate to the file on Google Drive. Option 1: Double-click the file to open the preview screen. At the top of the screen, click the “Open with Google Sheets” button. Option 2: Right-click the file. Select “Open with Google Sheets.” 2. Do Not Use Microsoft Excel Avoid downloading the spreadsheet and opening it in Microsoft Excel, as this disrupts the collaborative process. When a file is downloaded and edited in Excel, any changes made by other users during that time will not be reflected. Re-uploading the file to Google Drive will overwrite edits made by others, potentially causing data loss. 3. Avoid Duplicate Files Do not create duplicate versions of the spreadsheet in the shared drive. Multiple versions can cause confusion and result in updates being made to the wrong file. 4. Save and Refresh Google Sheets saves changes automatically in real-time. Refreshing the page ensures that changes from other collaborators are reflected in the file. Title: Measure Square layouts
Description: Hi Kolby, The sales team is having issues with layouts not showing up in measure square. It seems like their layouts are not synching to the cloud, but the issues is that its not showing up on their tablets either.
Resolution:
Hi everyone,

We have seen this problem before and it has to do with the avaliable memory on the device. The best solution is to make sure that no other app is running except MeasureSquare on the Tablet:

Alex, to do this, hit the 3 vertical lines at the bottom right of your tablet, |||. 

Then hit Close All to close all apps, then open MeasureSquare again. 

Do this anytime you plan on using MeasureSquare for the first time of the day or if it freezes at all. It should get you quickly back to work and it's unlikely you will lose any significant progress unless you were in the middle of drawing a room. 

Let me know how frequently this happens, if you can, make a note of how many times it freezed on a day you're out measuring and chat me, so I can determine if it's just tablet memory or a larger unforseen incompatibility.

Thank you,

Kollby

Title: Costing Sheet Error - Macros not working
Description: Marlene is having issues with the Costing Sheet, she is not able to generate the quotes after filling out the costing sheets. the macros are not working.
Resolution:
The issue with the costing sheet macros not working was identified as the file being saved as a regular Excel worksheet instead of a macro-enabled worksheet. 
I assisted Marlene in downloading the latest version of the costing sheet template and provided instructions on how to properly save the file using the "Save as" macro button to ensure it is saved in the correct format. 
Marlene was also advised to copy the data from the incorrectly saved file into a new costing sheet template and save it as a macro-enabled worksheet to restore functionality.

Title: PDF Subscription Manager
Description: Madlen in LA called to let us know that the LA PDF Subscription Manager is updating incorrectly for Sofi at Wood Ranch West and Sofi at Wood Ranch West - PUR. When updating the emails for West it updates the email to West - PUR and vice versa. Also, when you search for West and select it, West - PUR comes up instead. I believe there is an Insight account number issue causing this. We will need to look at the tables in SQL Insight to see what might be happening, possibly even in the SQL CUF Complex table as well.
Resolution:
The issue was due to an incorrect entry of the property name when entered into Insight.

When searching by property name, the selection made was "Sofi at Woodranch West". However, this did not match other properties in the system, which were entered with variations like "Sofi at Wood Ranch West PUR", "Sofi at Wood Ranch East", and "Sofi at Wood Ranch East PUR".

The absence of a space between "Wood" and "Ranch" in the selected name caused incorrect filtering results.

This has been rectified by updating the property name to the correct spelling: "Sofi at Wood Ranch West".
